physics_goals.value: Measure the flux of ultrahigh-energy cosmic rays and test for the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin suppression and the ankle.

summary.plain: HiRes was a pair of fluorescence telescopes in the Utah desert, a sharper successor to Fly's Eye. Operating 1997-2006, it reported the first observation of the Greisen-Zatsepin-Kuzmin suppression of the highest-energy cosmic rays.
summary.technical: Second-generation air-fluorescence experiment at Dugway Proving Ground: HiRes-I (22 telescope modules, 1997) and HiRes-II (42 modules with FADC readout, 1999), 12.6 km apart, 1 degree PMT pixels, 3.7 m2 mirrors. Measured the UHECR flux by monocular and stereo techniques; observed the ankle (4 × 10¹⁸ eV) and the GZK suppression (6 × 10¹⁹ eV) at 5 sigma.
